classification.difficultyReason: Classify triangles directly from supplied angles, side ticks, equal-angle symbols and their appearance.

content.prompt: Classify these triangles. Circle every description that matches.

spec.description: Triangle with 55° at lower left, 42° at upper right and 83° at lower right.
spec.mathematics: Three distinct acute angles; no side ticks.
spec.answerVisibility: All angles are permanent givens. No classification answer is printed.

answer.worked:
The three angles are different, so the sides are all different: scalene. Each angle is less than $90^\circ$: acute.

Correct answer: Scalene, Acute.

spec.description: Triangle with 37° at lower left, 53° at the upper vertex and a right-angle square at lower right; two, one and three side ticks respectively.
spec.answerVisibility: Angles and side marks are permanent givens.

answer.worked:
The three different side marks show three different side lengths: scalene. The square marks a $90^\circ$ angle: right.

Correct answer: Scalene, Right.

spec.description: Right-pointing equilateral triangle with one tick on each side and all three angles labelled 60°.
spec.mathematics: All sides equal; three equal 60° angles.
spec.answerVisibility: Side ticks and angle labels remain visible.

answer.worked:
All three sides have the same tick: equilateral. Each angle is $60^\circ$, less than $90^\circ$: acute.

Correct answer: Equilateral, Acute.

spec.description: Right-pointing triangle with upper-left angle 78°, other angles 51°, two equal single-ticked sides and a double-ticked opposite side.
spec.mathematics: Two equal sides; all angles acute.
spec.answerVisibility: All labels and ticks are permanent givens.

answer.worked:
Two sides have the same tick: isosceles. The angles $78^\circ$, $51^\circ$ and $51^\circ$ are all less than $90^\circ$: acute.

Correct answer: Isosceles, Acute.

spec.description: Wide triangle with upper angle 110°, two lower angles 35°, single ticks on the two upper sides and double ticks on the base.
spec.mathematics: Two equal sides and an obtuse apex angle.
spec.answerVisibility: All labels and ticks are permanent givens.

answer.worked:
Two sides have the same tick: isosceles. The $110^\circ$ angle is greater than $90^\circ$: obtuse.

Correct answer: Isosceles, Obtuse.

spec.description: Right-pointing triangle with a right-angle square at upper left and one, two and three ticks on its three sides.
spec.mathematics: The upper-left sides are perpendicular; all side lengths differ.
spec.answerVisibility: Right-angle square and side marks remain visible.

answer.worked:
The three different side marks show three different side lengths: scalene. The square marks a $90^\circ$ angle: right.

Correct answer: Scalene, Right.

spec.description: Triangle with equal vertical and horizontal legs, one tick on each leg and a right-angle square at lower left.
spec.mathematics: Two equal perpendicular sides; diagonal unmarked.

answer.worked:
Two sides have the same tick: isosceles. The square marks a $90^\circ$ angle: right.

Correct answer: Isosceles, Right.

spec.description: Triangle with 95° at upper right, matching single ticks on the sides meeting there, and double ticks on the opposite side.
spec.mathematics: Equal adjacent sides enclose an angle of 95°.
spec.answerVisibility: The 95° label and all ticks remain visible; no additional angle arc is supplied.

answer.worked:
Two sides have the same tick: isosceles. The $95^\circ$ angle is greater than $90^\circ$: obtuse.

Correct answer: Isosceles, Obtuse.

spec.description: Upright triangle with horizontal base and one tick on every side.
spec.mathematics: All three sides equal; no numerical angles supplied.

answer.worked:
All three sides have the same tick: equilateral. An equilateral triangle has three $60^\circ$ angles, all less than $90^\circ$: acute.

Correct answer: Equilateral, Acute.

spec.description: Right-pointing triangle with approximately vertical left side and one matching arc at every interior angle.
spec.mathematics: All three angles equal; no side ticks or numerical angle labels.

answer.worked:
The matching arcs show three equal angles, so all three sides are equal: equilateral. Each angle is $60^\circ$, less than $90^\circ$: acute.

Correct answer: Equilateral, Acute.

spec.description: Triangle with cross at lower left, solid dot at upper vertex and hollow circle at lower right.
spec.mathematics: Distinct angle identifiers indicate unequal angles; the source drawing shows three acute angles. Coordinates reconstruct appearance and are not additional givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Identifiers remain visible; no numerical angles are added.

answer.worked:
The different angle symbols indicate three different angles, so all sides are different: scalene. The drawing shows each angle less than $90^\circ$: acute.

Correct answer: Scalene, Acute.

spec.description: Long sloping triangle with equal solid-dot angle identifiers at lower left and upper right; lower-right angle unmarked and visibly obtuse.
spec.mathematics: Matching angle identifiers imply two equal opposite sides. Coordinates preserve an obtuse lower-right angle without supplying a numerical angle.

answer.worked:
The matching dots show two equal angles, so their opposite sides are equal: isosceles. The drawing shows the lower-right angle greater than $90^\circ$: obtuse.

Correct answer: Isosceles, Obtuse.
